note: Atoms are the primitives. Every pattern in this atlas instantiates one or more. New atoms require an explicit decision.

atoms.name: interpreter confusion
atoms.definition: untrusted data is treated as inert by one layer and as code or syntax by another
atoms.signal: a parser receives data the first layer thought was data
atoms.mitigation: context aware encoding at the exact sink, never before it

atoms.name: trust boundary crossing
atoms.definition: a lower privileged principal causes an action with higher privilege authority
atoms.signal: an object or action succeeds for a principal that should not own it
atoms.mitigation: object level and function level checks on every path, deny by default

atoms.name: identity confusion
atoms.definition: the system misidentifies who or what is acting
atoms.mitigation: one identity resolution point, explicit audience, no identity from headers

atoms.name: state confusion
atoms.definition: the system's view of state differs from real state
atoms.mitigation: single source of truth, idempotency keys, transactional state

atoms.name: type and shape confusion
atoms.definition: a value is valid in one context and means something else in another
atoms.signal: the same bytes parse differently in two places
atoms.mitigation: schema validation at every boundary, explicit allowlists

atoms.name: path and namespace confusion
atoms.definition: two components resolve the same name or path to different targets
atoms.signal: what the validator checked is not what the handler used
atoms.mitigation: canonicalise once, compare canonical forms, no path from user input

atoms.name: resource exhaustion
atoms.definition: a finite resource is consumed faster than it is replenished
atoms.signal: latency, error rate or cost spikes under cheap input
atoms.mitigation: cost analysis per operation, quotas by principal

atoms.name: information exposure
atoms.definition: data reaches a party that should not receive it
atoms.signal: an unexpected channel carries protected data
atoms.mitigation: egress allowlist, response shaping, uniform errors

atoms.name: cryptographic weakness
atoms.definition: a property the design assumes is true is not
atoms.signal: crypto behaviour contradicts its stated guarantee
atoms.mitigation: vetted libraries, fixed algorithms, no negotiation from input

atoms.name: logic assumption violation
atoms.definition: the workflow relies on an invariant the attacker can break
atoms.signal: the system does something valid per field but wrong per business rule
atoms.mitigation: invariants enforced server side per step, not per field

atoms.name: dependency compromise
atoms.definition: an upstream artifact is trusted and should not be
atoms.signal: the build or runtime pulls code nobody reviewed
atoms.mitigation: pinned digests, private registry priority, provenance, review

atoms.name: timing and ordering
atoms.definition: the window between check and use is exploitable

atoms.name: side channel
atoms.signal: a legitimate observable reveals a secret
atoms.mitigation: constant time compare, uniform responses, no secret dependent branching

atoms.name: human manipulation
atoms.definition: the human in the loop is the weakest component
atoms.signal: a person takes an action they would not have taken informed
atoms.mitigation: phishing resistant auth, process with out of band verification

atoms.name: configuration divergence
atoms.definition: the deployed state differs from the intended state
atoms.signal: the system behaves per an unstated default
atoms.mitigation: config as code with drift detection, secure defaults audited

atoms.name: model and agent manipulation
atoms.definition: an AI component's instruction following is the trust boundary
atoms.signal: the model does something the operator did not intend
atoms.mitigation: treat retrieved text as data, least privilege tools, output validation
